title: You didn’t drift.
paragraphs: And now you don’t know how to come back.
Because it wasn’t just a mistake.

A moment you replay at night when everything goes quiet…
and your soul whispers,
“God saw that.”

To pray.
To worship.
To even look up.
“Maybe I went too far this time.”
Let me meet you right there.
In Genesis 3:8, when Adam and Eve sinned, they did something instinctive:
“They hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God…”

They covered.
They avoided.
They ran.
But because they were lost in shame.
And you are doing the same thing right now.
But you don’t want Him to see that part of you.

You scroll.
You distract.
You pretend.

Worship on the outside.
Compromise in the shadows.

Smiling in public.
Breaking in private.
“The wages of sin is death…” — Romans 6:23

Spiritual numbness.
Emotional heaviness.
Distance from God.
Some scholars interpret this “death” not only as eternal separation, but also the slow decay of joy, peace, and identity even while you’re still breathing.
You think your sin disqualified you.
God says it revealed your need for a Savior.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8

Not after you fixed it.
Not after you cleaned up.
While you were still in it.
Jesus didn’t wait for your apology.
The cross was not God saying, “Get it together.”
That sin you think is too dark?
That secret you think disqualifies you?
Jesus carried it on His back.
That shame that keeps whispering, “Stay away”?
So why are you still trying to earn what He already purchased?
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us…” — 1 John 1:9

Not moody.
Not hesitant.
Not waiting to shame you.
Because Jesus already took your penalty.

You sinned.
You fell short.
You cannot save yourself.

lived the life you couldn’t live,
died the death you deserved,
rose again to give you new life.
How long will you stay in hiding…
when the door is already open?
God is not intimidated by your mess.
He’s inviting you out of it.
Close your eyes if you need to.

“Jesus… I’ve been running.
I confess my sin.
I turn back to You.
Cleanse me. Change me.
I surrender.”
